title: Language version recap, style, and performance — interview

items.question: Name C# 14 features you would actually use in a worker.
items.answer: Implicit span conversions when slicing payloads (module 17). field-backed properties when a setter must trim or notify without a manual backing field (module 04 recap). Null-conditional assignment when an optional customer object should not evaluate the right-hand side. nameof(List<>) in diagnostics. Extension members if you are writing a library API; skip them in a one-off consumer. I would not lead with interceptors — they stayed experimental from C# 12.
followUps: Which of those need a TFM bump versus only LangVersion?
items.sixtySeconds: C# 14: span conversions, field, ?. assignment, unbound nameof. C# 13: Lock, params Span. Need net10.0.

items.question: How do you choose LangVersion in csproj?
items.answer: Leave it to the TFM. net10.0 is C# 14. Override only for preview. Never latest. Directory.Build.props can pin a solution but C# and VB numbers differ. #error version prints the compiler’s choice. Language newer than TFM is unsupported because APIs may be missing.
followUps: Give a breaking change that appears when you raise the language.
What does the field keyword break?
items.sixtySeconds: TFM selects language. No latest. field can shadow a field named field. Read Roslyn breaking-change notes.

items.question: When is a record the wrong type for a domain entity?
items.answer: When identity is not structural equality. An Attempt with the same scores is not the same attempt. Records give value equality, with-expressions, and positional constructors — perfect for a Redis DTO or a CSV row you parsed. A domain entity needs a constructor that enforces invariants, maybe mutation behind methods, and reference identity. Mixing them leaks with-clones that skip validation.
followUps: How does that interact with Span parsing?
items.sixtySeconds: Record = value shape. Entity = identity plus invariants. DTO = serialization. Do not with-clone around validation.

items.question: What do you look for first in a C# PR during an interview?
items.answer: Lifetime: missing Dispose on SkiaSharp-like handles, Span across await, fire-and-forget async. Then allocations on a hot path: Split on CSV, extra ToList on LINQ (modules 12 and 17). Then accidental public API (module 16). Then naming and leftover experimental syntax. I talk through that order so the interviewer sees judgment, not a lint dump.
followUps: How would you block the public API issue in CI?
What is a five-year-engineer tell in naming?
items.sixtySeconds: Dispose and async first. Then GC. Then public surface. Style last. Cite modules, do not re-teach them.
